summary: Invalidation is hard because every write path must drop the same key the read path uses. Caching auth-protected rows would leak across principals. If Redis is down we fall back to the store — already proven REDIS_DOWN True with 307.
evidence: Invalidation: PATCH must call invalidate_redirect_target(code) or GET /r/{code} keeps the old Location. We proved STALE_AVOIDED True only after that call; skipping it is the BREAK we will inject.
Auth-protected data: we cache only public redirect targets (code->long_url), never principal-scoped GET /links/{code} bodies. Caching A's analytics under a shared key would be IDOR via cache.
Redis unavailable: redis-py ping with 0.2s timeout failed; LOG_REDIS_DOWN_FALLBACK True; redirect still 307 from memory SoT. We did not hang and did not fabricate a Redis HIT.
